texts.jas.4.14: Digo-vos que não sabeis o que acontecerá ámanhã. Porque, que é a vossa vida? É um vapor que apparece por um pouco, e depois se desvanece.
texts.jas.4.15: Em logar do que devieis dizer: Se o Senhor quizer, e se vivermos, faremos isto ou aquillo.
texts.jas.4.16: Mas agora vos gloriaes em vossas presumpções: toda a gloria tal como esta é maligna.
texts.jas.4.17: Aquelle pois que sabe fazer o bem e o não faz commette peccado.
texts.jas.5.1: Eia pois agora vós, ricos, chorae e pranteae, por vossas miserias, que sobre vós hão de vir.
texts.jas.5.2: As vossas riquezas estão apodrecidas, e os vossos vestidos estão comidos da traça.
texts.jas.5.3: O vosso oiro e a vossa prata se enferrujaram; e a sua ferrugem dará testemunho contra vós, e comerá como fogo a vossa carne. Enthesourastes para os ultimos dias.
texts.jas.5.4: Eis que o jornal dos trabalhadores que ceifaram as vossas terras, e o qual por vós foi diminuido, clama; e os clamores dos que ceifaram entraram nos ouvidos do Senhor dos exercitos.
texts.jas.5.5: Deliciosamente vivestes sobre a terra, e vos deleitastes: cevastes os vossos corações, como n’um dia de matança.
texts.jas.5.6: Condemnastes e matastes o justo; elle não vos resistiu.
texts.jas.5.7: Sêde pois, irmãos, pacientes até á vinda do Senhor. Eis que o lavrador espera o precioso fructo da terra, aguardando-o com paciencia, até que receba a chuva temporã e serodia.
texts.jas.5.8: Sêde vós tambem pacientes, fortalecei os vossos corações; porque já a vinda do Senhor está proxima.
texts.jas.5.9: Irmãos, não vos queixeis uns contra os outros, para que não sejaes condemnados. Eis que o juiz está á porta.
texts.jas.5.10: Meus irmãos, tomae por exemplo de afflicção e paciencia os prophetas que fallaram em nome do Senhor.
texts.jas.5.11: Eis que temos por bemaventurados os que soffrem. Ouvistes qual foi a paciencia de Job, e vistes o fim que o Senhor lhe deu; porque o Senhor é muito misericordioso e piedoso.
texts.jas.5.12: Porém, sobretudo, meus irmãos, não jureis, nem pelo céu, nem pela terra, nem façaes qualquer outro juramento; mas que a vossa palavra seja sim, sim, e não, não; para que não caiaes em condemnação.
texts.jas.5.13: Está alguem entre vós afflicto? ore. Está alguem contente? psalmodie.
texts.jas.5.14: Está alguem entre vós doente? chame os anciãos da egreja, e orem sobre elle, ungindo-o com azeite em nome do Senhor;
texts.jas.5.15: E a oração da fé salvará o doente, e o Senhor o levantará; e, se houver commettido peccados, ser-lhe-hão perdoados.
texts.jas.5.16: Confessae as vossas culpas uns aos outros, e orae uns pelos outros para que sareis: a oração efficaz do justo pode muito.
texts.jas.5.17: Elias era homem sujeito ás mesmas paixões que nós, e, orando, pediu que não chovesse, e, por tres annos e seis mezes, não choveu sobre a terra.
texts.jas.5.18: E orou outra vez, e o céu deu chuva, e a terra produziu o seu fructo.
texts.jas.5.19: Irmãos, se algum de entre vós se tem desviado da verdade, e algum o converter,
texts.jas.5.20: Saiba que aquelle que fizer converter do erro do seu caminho um peccador salvará da morte uma alma, e cobrirá uma multidão de peccados.

texts.jas.1.1: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.
texts.jas.1.2: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.
texts.jas.1.3: Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.
texts.jas.1.4: But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
texts.jas.1.5: If any of you lacketh wisdom, let him ask of God, who giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given to him.
texts.jas.1.6: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
texts.jas.1.7: For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing from the Lord.
texts.jas.1.8: A man unsettled in his opinions is unstable in all his ways.
texts.jas.1.9: Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:
texts.jas.1.10: But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.
texts.jas.1.11: For the sun hath no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and its flower falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.
texts.jas.1.12: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.
texts.jas.1.13: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted by God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:
texts.jas.1.14: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away by his own lust, and enticed.
texts.jas.1.15: Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.
texts.jas.1.16: Do not err, my beloved brethren.
texts.jas.1.17: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
texts.jas.1.18: Of his own will he hath begotten us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first-fruits of his creatures.
texts.jas.1.19: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
texts.jas.1.20: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.
texts.jas.1.21: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the ingrafted word, which is able to save your souls.
texts.jas.1.22: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
texts.jas.1.23: For if any is a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like a man beholding his natural face in a glass:
texts.jas.1.24: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth away, and immediately forgetteth what manner of man he was.
texts.jas.1.25: But he who looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth in it, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.
texts.jas.1.26: If any man among you seemeth to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain.
texts.jas.1.27: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
texts.jas.2.1: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.
texts.jas.2.2: For if there come into your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;
texts.jas.2.3: And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say to him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:
texts.jas.2.4: Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?
texts.jas.2.5: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?
texts.jas.2.6: But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment-seats?
texts.jas.2.7: Do they not blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?
texts.jas.2.8: If ye fulfill the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself, ye do well:
texts.jas.2.9: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
texts.jas.2.10: For whoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
texts.jas.2.11: For he that said, Do not commit adultery; said also, Do not kill. Now if thou committest no adultery, yet if thou killest, thou art become a transgressor of the law.
texts.jas.2.12: So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.
texts.jas.2.13: For he shall have judgment without mercy that hath shown no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.
texts.jas.2.14: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man sayeth he hath faith, and hath not works? can faith save him?
texts.jas.2.15: If a brother or sister is naked, and destitute of daily food,
texts.jas.2.16: And one of you sayeth to them, Depart in peace, be you warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?
texts.jas.2.17: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
texts.jas.2.18: Also a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: show me thy faith without thy works, and I will show thee my faith by my works.
texts.jas.2.19: Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the demons also believe, and tremble.
texts.jas.2.20: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?
texts.jas.2.21: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
texts.jas.2.22: Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?
texts.jas.2.23: And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.
texts.jas.2.24: Ye see then that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.
texts.jas.2.25: Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
texts.jas.2.26: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
texts.jas.3.1: My brethren, be not many teachers, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.
texts.jas.3.2: For in many things we all offend. If any man offendeth not in word, the same is a perfect man, able also to bridle the whole body.
texts.jas.3.3: Behold, we put bits in the mouths of horses, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.
texts.jas.3.4: Behold also the ships, which though they are so great, and are driven by fierce winds, yet they are turned about with a very small helm, withersoever the governor willeth.
texts.jas.3.5: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!
texts.jas.3.6: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire from hell.
texts.jas.3.7: For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of animals in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed by mankind:
texts.jas.3.8: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
texts.jas.3.9: With this we bless God, even the Father; and with this we curse men, who are made after the similitude of God.
texts.jas.3.10: Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.
texts.jas.3.11: Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter?
texts.jas.3.12: Can the fig-tree, my brethren, bear olive-berries? or a vine, figs? so no fountain can yield both salt water and fresh.
texts.jas.3.13: Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him show by a good deportment his works with meekness of wisdom.
texts.jas.3.14: But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.
texts.jas.3.15: This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, demoniacal.
texts.jas.3.16: For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.
texts.jas.3.17: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
texts.jas.3.18: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by them that make peace.
texts.jas.4.1: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even from your lusts that war in your members?
texts.jas.4.2: Ye lust and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.
texts.jas.4.3: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.
texts.jas.4.4: Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.
texts.jas.4.5: Do ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy?
texts.jas.4.6: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace to the humble.
texts.jas.4.7: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
texts.jas.4.8: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners, and purify your hearts, ye double-minded.
texts.jas.4.9: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness.
texts.jas.4.10: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will lift you up.
texts.jas.4.11: Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaketh evil of his brother, and judgeth his brother, speaketh evil of the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judgest the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.
texts.jas.4.12: There is one lawgiver, who is able to save, and to destroy: who art thou that judgest another?
texts.jas.4.13: Come now, ye that say, To-day or to-morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy, and sell, and get gain:
texts.jas.4.14: Whereas ye know not what will be on the morrow: For what is your life? It is even a vapor, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
texts.jas.4.15: Instead of that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.
texts.jas.4.16: But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.
texts.jas.4.17: Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.
texts.jas.5.1: Come now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.
texts.jas.5.2: Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are moth-eaten.
texts.jas.5.3: Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a testimony against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have amassed treasure for the last days.
texts.jas.5.4: Behold, the hire of the laborers who have reaped your fields, which is by you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them who have reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.
texts.jas.5.5: Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.
texts.jas.5.6: Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.
texts.jas.5.7: Be patient, therefore, brethren, to the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receiveth the early and the latter rain.
texts.jas.5.8: Be ye also patient; establish your hearts; for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh.
texts.jas.5.9: Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned: behold, the judge standeth before the door.
texts.jas.5.10: Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience.
texts.jas.5.11: Behold, we count them happy who endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.
texts.jas.5.12: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea, be yea: and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.
texts.jas.5.13: Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any cheerful? let him sing psalms.
texts.jas.5.14: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:
texts.jas.5.15: And the prayer of faith will save the sick, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he hath committed sins, they will be forgiven him.
texts.jas.5.16: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of the righteous man availeth much.
texts.jas.5.17: Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months.
texts.jas.5.18: And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
texts.jas.5.19: Brethren, if any one of you should err from the truth, and one should convert him;
texts.jas.5.20: Let him know, that he who converteth a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death, and will hide a multitude of sins.

texts.jas.1.1: James, bondman of God and of [the] Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which [are] in the dispersion, greeting.
texts.jas.1.2: Count it all joy, my brethren, when ye fall into various temptations,
texts.jas.1.3: knowing that the proving of your faith works endurance.
texts.jas.1.4: But let endurance have [its] perfect work, that ye may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
texts.jas.1.5: But if any one of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all freely and reproaches not, and it shall be given to him:
texts.jas.1.6: but let him ask in faith, nothing doubting. For he that doubts is like a wave of the sea driven by the wind and tossed about;
texts.jas.1.7: for let not that man think that he shall receive anything from the Lord;
texts.jas.1.8: [he is] a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
texts.jas.1.9: But let the brother of low degree glory in his elevation,
texts.jas.1.10: and the rich in his humiliation, because as [the] grass's flower he will pass away.
texts.jas.1.11: For the sun has risen with its burning heat, and has withered the grass, and its flower has fallen, and the comeliness of its look has perished: thus the rich also shall wither in his goings.
texts.jas.1.12: Blessed [is the] man who endures temptation; for, having been proved, he shall receive the crown of life, which He has promised to them that love him.
texts.jas.1.13: Let no man, being tempted, say, I am tempted of God. For God cannot be tempted by evil things, and himself tempts no one.
texts.jas.1.14: But every one is tempted, drawn away, and enticed by his own lust;
texts.jas.1.15: then lust, having conceived, gives birth to sin; but sin fully completed brings forth death.
texts.jas.1.16: Do not err, my beloved brethren.
texts.jas.1.17: Every good gift and every perfect gift comes down from above, from the Father of lights, with whom is no variation nor shadow of turning.
texts.jas.1.18: According to his own will begat he us by the word of truth, that we should be a certain first-fruits of *his* creatures.
texts.jas.1.19: So that, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath;
texts.jas.1.20: for man's wrath does not work God's righteousness.
texts.jas.1.21: Wherefore, laying aside all filthiness and abounding of wickedness, accept with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
texts.jas.1.22: But be ye doers of [the] word and not hearers only, beguiling yourselves.
texts.jas.1.23: For if any man be a hearer of [the] word and not a doer, *he* is like to a man considering his natural face in a mirror:
texts.jas.1.24: for he has considered himself and is gone away, and straightway he has forgotten what he was like.
texts.jas.1.25: But *he* that fixes his view on [the] perfect law, that of liberty, and abides in [it], being not a forgetful hearer but a doer of [the] work, *he* shall be blessed in his doing.
texts.jas.1.26: If any one think himself to be religious, not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his heart, this man's religion is vain.
texts.jas.1.27: Pure and undefiled religion before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, to keep oneself unspotted from the world.
texts.jas.2.1: My brethren, do not have the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Lord] of glory, with respect of persons:
texts.jas.2.2: for if there come unto your synagogue a man with a gold ring in splendid apparel, and a poor man also come in in vile apparel,
texts.jas.2.3: and ye look upon him who wears the splendid apparel, and say, Do thou sit here well, and say to the poor, Do thou stand there, or sit here under my footstool:
texts.jas.2.4: have ye not made a difference among yourselves, and become judges having evil thoughts?
texts.jas.2.5: Hear, my beloved brethren: Has not God chosen the poor as to the world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom, which he has promised to them that love him?
texts.jas.2.6: But *ye* have despised the poor [man]. Do not the rich oppress you, and [do not] *they* drag you before [the] tribunals?
texts.jas.2.7: And [do not] *they* blaspheme the excellent name which has been called upon you?
texts.jas.2.8: If indeed ye keep [the] royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well.
texts.jas.2.9: But if ye have respect of persons, ye commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
texts.jas.2.10: For whoever shall keep the whole law and shall offend in one [point], he has come under the guilt of [breaking] all.
texts.jas.2.11: For he who said, Thou shalt not commit adultery, said also, Thou shalt not kill. Now if thou dost not commit adultery, but killest, thou art become transgressor of [the] law.
texts.jas.2.12: So speak ye, and so act, as those that are to be judged by [the] law of liberty;
texts.jas.2.13: for judgment [will be] without mercy to him that has shewn no mercy. Mercy glories over judgment.
texts.jas.2.14: What [is] the profit, my brethren, if any one say he have faith, but have not works? can faith save him?
texts.jas.2.15: Now if a brother or a sister is naked and destitute of daily food,
texts.jas.2.16: and one from amongst you say to them, Go in peace, be warmed and filled; but give not to them the needful things for the body, what [is] the profit?
texts.jas.2.17: So also faith, if it have not works, is dead by itself.
texts.jas.2.18: But some one will say, *Thou* hast faith and *I* have works. Shew me thy faith without works, and *I* from my works will shew thee my faith.
texts.jas.2.19: *Thou* believest that God is one. Thou doest well. The demons even believe, and tremble.
texts.jas.2.20: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?
texts.jas.2.21: Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
texts.jas.2.22: Thou seest that faith wrought with his works, and that by works faith was perfected.
texts.jas.2.23: And the scripture was fulfilled which says, Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness, and he was called Friend of God.
texts.jas.2.24: Ye see that a man is justified on the principle of works, and not on the principle of faith only.
texts.jas.2.25: But was not in like manner also Rahab the harlot justified on the principle of works, when she had received the messengers and put [them] forth by another way?
texts.jas.2.26: For as the body without a spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
texts.jas.3.1: Be not many teachers, my brethren, knowing that we shall receive greater judgment.
texts.jas.3.2: For we all often offend. If any one offend not in word, *he* [is] a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body too.
texts.jas.3.3: Behold, we put the bits in the mouths of the horses, that they may obey us, and we turn round their whole bodies.
texts.jas.3.4: Behold also the ships, which are so great, and driven by violent winds, are turned about by a very small rudder, wherever the pleasure of the helmsman will.
texts.jas.3.5: Thus also the tongue is a little member, and boasts great things. See how little a fire, how large a wood it kindles!
texts.jas.3.6: and the tongue [is] fire, the world of unrighteousness; the tongue is set in our members, the defiler of the whole body, and which sets fire to the course of nature, and is set on fire of hell.
texts.jas.3.7: For every species both of beasts and of birds, both of creeping things and of sea animals, is tamed and has been tamed by the human species;
texts.jas.3.8: but the tongue can no one among men tame; [it is] an unsettled evil, full of death-bringing poison.
texts.jas.3.9: Therewith bless we the Lord and Father, and therewith curse we men made after [the] likeness of God.
texts.jas.3.10: Out of the same mouth goes forth blessing and cursing. It is not right, my brethren, that these things should be thus.
texts.jas.3.11: Does the fountain, out of the same opening, pour forth sweet and bitter?
texts.jas.3.12: Can, my brethren, a fig produce olives, or a vine figs? Neither [can] salt [water] make sweet water.
texts.jas.3.13: Who [is] wise and understanding among you; let him shew out of a good conversation his works in meekness of wisdom;
texts.jas.3.14: but if ye have bitter emulation and strife in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth.
texts.jas.3.15: This is not the wisdom which comes down from above, but earthly, natural, devilish.
texts.jas.3.16: For where emulation and strife [are], there [is] disorder and every evil thing.
texts.jas.3.17: But the wisdom from above first is pure, then peaceful, gentle, yielding, full of mercy and good fruits, unquestioning, unfeigned.
texts.jas.3.18: But [the] fruit of righteousness in peace is sown for them that make peace.
texts.jas.4.1: Whence [come] wars and whence fightings among you? [Is it] not thence, -- from your pleasures, which war in your members?
texts.jas.4.2: Ye lust and have not: ye kill and are full of envy, and cannot obtain; ye fight and war; ye have not because ye ask not.
texts.jas.4.3: Ye ask and receive not, because ye ask evilly, that ye may consume [it] in your pleasures.
texts.jas.4.4: Adulteresses, know ye not that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Whoever therefore is minded to be [the] friend of the world is constituted enemy of God.
texts.jas.4.5: Think ye that the scripture speaks in vain? Does the Spirit which has taken his abode in us desire enviously?
texts.jas.4.6: But he gives more grace. Wherefore he says, God sets himself against [the] proud, but gives grace to [the] lowly.
texts.jas.4.7: Subject yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
texts.jas.4.8: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse [your] hands, sinners, and purify [your] hearts, ye double-minded.
texts.jas.4.9: Be wretched, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and [your] joy to heaviness.
texts.jas.4.10: Humble yourselves before [the] Lord, and he shall exalt you.
texts.jas.4.11: Speak not against one another, brethren. He that speaks against [his] brother, or judges his brother, speaks against [the] law and judges [the] law. But if thou judgest [the] law, thou art not doer of [the] law, but judge.
texts.jas.4.12: One is the lawgiver and judge, who is able to save and to destroy: but who art *thou* who judgest thy neighbour?
texts.jas.4.13: Go to now, ye who say, To-day or to-morrow will we go into such a city and spend a year there, and traffic and make gain,
texts.jas.4.14: ye who do not know what will be on the morrow, ([for] what [is] your life? It is even a vapour, appearing for a little while, and then disappearing,)
texts.jas.4.15: instead of your saying, If the Lord should [so] will and we should live, we will also do this or that.
texts.jas.4.16: But now ye glory in your vauntings: all such glorying is evil.
texts.jas.4.17: To him therefore who knows how to do good, and does it not, to him it is sin.
texts.jas.5.1: Go to now, ye rich, weep, howling over your miseries that [are] coming upon [you].
texts.jas.5.2: Your wealth is become rotten, and your garments moth-eaten.
texts.jas.5.3: Your gold and silver is eaten away, and their canker shall be for a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as fire. Ye have heaped up treasure in [the] last days.
texts.jas.5.4: Behold, the wages of your labourers, who have harvested your fields, wrongfully kept back by you, cry, and the cries of those that have reaped are entered into the ears of [the] Lord of sabaoth.
texts.jas.5.5: Ye have lived luxuriously on the earth and indulged yourselves; ye have nourished your hearts [as] in a day of slaughter;
texts.jas.5.6: ye have condemned, ye have killed the just; he does not resist you.
texts.jas.5.7: Have patience, therefore, brethren, till the coming of the Lord. Behold, the labourer awaits the precious fruit of the earth, having patience for it until it receive [the] early and [the] latter rain.
texts.jas.5.8: *Ye* also have patience: stablish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is drawn nigh.
texts.jas.5.9: Complain not one against another, brethren, that ye be not judged. Behold, the judge stands before the door.
texts.jas.5.10: Take [as] an example, brethren, of suffering and having patience, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of [the] Lord.
texts.jas.5.11: Behold, we call them blessed who have endured. Ye have heard of the endurance of Job, and seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is full of tender compassion and pitiful.
texts.jas.5.12: But before all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by any other oath; but let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay, that ye do not fall under judgment.
texts.jas.5.13: Does any one among you suffer evil? let him pray. Is any happy? let him sing psalms.
texts.jas.5.14: Is any sick among you? let him call to [him] the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of [the] Lord;
texts.jas.5.15: and the prayer of faith shall heal the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he be one who has committed sins, it shall be forgiven him.
texts.jas.5.16: Confess therefore your offences to one another, and pray for one another, that ye may be healed. [The] fervent supplication of the righteous [man] has much power.
texts.jas.5.17: Elias was a man of like passions to us, and he prayed with prayer that it should not rain; and it did not rain upon the earth three years and six months;
texts.jas.5.18: and again he prayed, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth caused its fruit to spring forth.
texts.jas.5.19: My brethren, if any one among you err from the truth, and one bring him back,
texts.jas.5.20: let him know that he that brings back a sinner from [the] error of his way shall save a soul from death and shall cover a multitude of sins.

texts.jas.1.1: James, of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ a servant, to the Twelve Tribes who are in the dispersion: Hail!
texts.jas.1.2: All joy count [it], my brethren, when ye may fall into temptations manifold;
texts.jas.1.3: knowing that the proof of your faith doth work endurance,
texts.jas.1.4: and let the endurance have a perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire -- in nothing lacking;
texts.jas.1.5: and if any of you do lack wisdom, let him ask from God, who is giving to all liberally, and not reproaching, and it shall be given to him;
texts.jas.1.6: and let him ask in faith, nothing doubting, for he who is doubting hath been like a wave of the sea, driven by wind and tossed,
texts.jas.1.7: for let not that man suppose that he shall receive anything from the Lord --
texts.jas.1.8: a two-souled man [is] unstable in all his ways.
texts.jas.1.9: And let the brother who is low rejoice in his exaltation,
texts.jas.1.10: and the rich in his becoming low, because as a flower of grass he shall pass away;
texts.jas.1.11: for the sun did rise with the burning heat, and did wither the grass, and the flower of it fell, and the grace of its appearance did perish, so also the rich in his way shall fade away!
texts.jas.1.12: Happy the man who doth endure temptation, because, becoming approved, he shall receive the crown of the life, which the Lord did promise to those loving Him.
texts.jas.1.13: Let no one say, being tempted -- `From God I am tempted,' for God is not tempted of evil, and Himself doth tempt no one,
texts.jas.1.14: and each one is tempted, by his own desires being led away and enticed,
texts.jas.1.15: afterward the desire having conceived, doth give birth to sin, and the sin having been perfected, doth bring forth death.
texts.jas.1.16: Be not led astray, my brethren beloved;
texts.jas.1.17: every good giving, and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the lights, with whom is no variation, or shadow of turning;
texts.jas.1.18: having counselled, He did beget us with a word of truth, for our being a certain first-fruit of His creatures.
texts.jas.1.19: So then, my brethren beloved, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,
texts.jas.1.20: for the wrath of a man the righteousness of God doth not work;
texts.jas.1.21: wherefore having put aside all filthiness and superabundance of evil, in meekness be receiving the engrafted word, that is able to save your souls;
texts.jas.1.22: and become ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves,
texts.jas.1.23: because, if any one is a hearer of the word and not a doer, this one hath been like to a man viewing his natural face in a mirror,
texts.jas.1.24: for he did view himself, and hath gone away, and immediately he did forget of what kind he was;
texts.jas.1.25: and he who did look into the perfect law -- that of liberty, and did continue there, this one -- not a forgetful hearer becoming, but a doer of work -- this one shall be happy in his doing.
texts.jas.1.26: If any one doth think to be religious among you, not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his heart, of this one vain [is] the religion;
texts.jas.1.27: religion pure and undefiled with the God and Father is this, to look after orphans and widows in their tribulation -- unspotted to keep himself from the world.
texts.jas.2.1: My brethren, hold not, in respect of persons, the faith of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ,
texts.jas.2.2: for if there may come into your synagogue a man with gold ring, in gay raiment, and there may come in also a poor man in vile raiment,
texts.jas.2.3: and ye may look upon him bearing the gay raiment, and may say to him, `Thou -- sit thou here well,' and to the poor man may say, `Thou -- stand thou there, or, Sit thou here under my footstool,' --
texts.jas.2.4: ye did not judge fully in yourselves, and did become ill-reasoning judges.
texts.jas.2.5: Hearken, my brethren beloved, did not God choose the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the reign that He promised to those loving Him?
texts.jas.2.6: and ye did dishonour the poor one; do not the rich oppress you and themselves draw you to judgment-seats;
texts.jas.2.7: do they not themselves speak evil of the good name that was called upon you?
texts.jas.2.8: If, indeed, royal law ye complete, according to the Writing, `Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself,' -- ye do well;
texts.jas.2.9: and if ye accept persons, sin ye do work, being convicted by the law as transgressors;
texts.jas.2.10: for whoever the whole law shall keep, and shall stumble in one [point], he hath become guilty of all;
texts.jas.2.11: for He who is saying, `Thou mayest not commit adultery,' said also, `Thou mayest do no murder;' and if thou shalt not commit adultery, and shalt commit murder, thou hast become a transgressor of law;
texts.jas.2.12: so speak ye and so do, as about by a law of liberty to be judged,
texts.jas.2.13: for the judgment without kindness [is] to him not having done kindness, and exult doth kindness over judgment.
texts.jas.2.14: What [is] the profit, my brethren, if faith, any one may speak of having, and works he may not have? is that faith able to save him?
texts.jas.2.15: and if a brother or sister may be naked, and may be destitute of the daily food,
texts.jas.2.16: and any one of you may say to them, `Depart ye in peace, be warmed, and be filled,' and may not give to them the things needful for the body, what [is] the profit?
texts.jas.2.17: so also the faith, if it may not have works, is dead by itself.
texts.jas.2.18: But say may some one, Thou hast faith, and I have works, shew me thy faith out of thy works, and I will shew thee out of my works my faith:
texts.jas.2.19: thou -- thou dost believe that God is one; thou dost well, and the demons believe, and they shudder!
texts.jas.2.20: And dost thou wish to know, O vain man, that the faith apart from the works is dead?
texts.jas.2.21: Abraham our father -- was not he declared righteous out of works, having brought up Isaac his son upon the altar?
texts.jas.2.22: dost thou see that the faith was working with his works, and out of the works the faith was perfected?
texts.jas.2.23: and fulfilled was the Writing that is saying, `And Abraham did believe God, and it was reckoned to him -- to righteousness;' and, `Friend of God' he was called.
texts.jas.2.24: Ye see, then, that out of works is man declared righteous, and not out of faith only;
texts.jas.2.25: and in like manner also Rahab the harlot -- was she not out of works declared righteous, having received the messengers, and by another way having sent forth?
texts.jas.2.26: for as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also the faith apart from the works is dead.
texts.jas.3.1: Many teachers become not, my brethren, having known that greater judgment we shall receive,
texts.jas.3.2: for we all make many stumbles; if any one in word doth not stumble, this one [is] a perfect man, able to bridle also the whole body;
texts.jas.3.3: lo, the bits we put into the mouths of the horses for their obeying us, and their whole body we turn about;
texts.jas.3.4: lo, also the ships, being so great, and by fierce winds being driven, are led about by a very small helm, whithersoever the impulse of the helmsman doth counsel,
texts.jas.3.5: so also the tongue is a little member, and doth boast greatly; lo, a little fire how much wood it doth kindle!
texts.jas.3.6: and the tongue [is] a fire, the world of the unrighteousness, so the tongue is set in our members, which is spotting our whole body, and is setting on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by the gehenna.
texts.jas.3.7: For every nature, both of beasts and of fowls, both of creeping things and things of the sea, is subdued, and hath been subdued, by the human nature,
texts.jas.3.8: and the tongue no one of men is able to subdue, [it is] an unruly evil, full of deadly poison,
texts.jas.3.9: with it we do bless the God and Father, and with it we do curse the men made according to the similitude of God;
texts.jas.3.10: out of the same mouth doth come forth blessing and cursing; it doth not need, my brethren, these things so to happen;
texts.jas.3.11: doth the fountain out of the same opening pour forth the sweet and the bitter?
texts.jas.3.12: is a fig-tree able, my brethren, olives to make? or a vine figs? so no fountain salt and sweet water [is able] to make.
texts.jas.3.13: Who [is] wise and intelligent among you? let him shew out of the good behaviour his works in meekness of wisdom,
texts.jas.3.14: and if bitter zeal ye have, and rivalry in your heart, glory not, nor lie against the truth;
texts.jas.3.15: this wisdom is not descending from above, but earthly, physical, demon-like,
texts.jas.3.16: for where zeal and rivalry [are], there is insurrection and every evil matter;
texts.jas.3.17: and the wisdom from above, first, indeed, is pure, then peaceable, gentle, easily entreated, full of kindness and good fruits, uncontentious, and unhypocritical: --
texts.jas.3.18: and the fruit of the righteousness in peace is sown to those making peace.
texts.jas.4.1: Whence [are] wars and fightings among you? not thence -- out of your passions, that are as soldiers in your members?
texts.jas.4.2: ye desire, and ye have not; ye murder, and are zealous, and are not able to attain; ye fight and war, and ye have not, because of your not asking;
texts.jas.4.3: ye ask, and ye receive not, because evilly ye ask, that in your pleasures ye may spend [it].
texts.jas.4.4: Adulterers and adulteresses! have ye not known that friendship of the world is enmity with God? whoever, then, may counsel to be a friend of the world, an enemy of God he is set.
texts.jas.4.5: Do ye think that emptily the Writing saith, `To envy earnestly desireth the spirit that did dwell in us,'
texts.jas.4.6: and greater grace he doth give, wherefore he saith, `God against proud ones doth set Himself up, and to lowly ones He doth give grace?'
texts.jas.4.7: be subject, then, to God; stand up against the devil, and he will flee from you;
texts.jas.4.8: draw nigh to God, and He will draw nigh to you; cleanse hands, ye sinners! and purify hearts, ye two-souled!
texts.jas.4.9: be exceeding afflicted, and mourn, and weep, let your laughter to mourning be turned, and the joy to heaviness;
texts.jas.4.10: be made low before the Lord, and He shall exalt you.
texts.jas.4.11: Speak not one against another, brethren; he who is speaking against a brother, and is judging his brother, doth speak against law, and doth judge law, and if law thou dost judge, thou art not a doer of law but a judge;
texts.jas.4.12: one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy; thou -- who art thou that dost judge the other?
texts.jas.4.13: Go, now, ye who are saying, `To-day and to-morrow we will go on to such a city, and will pass there one year, and traffic, and make gain;'
texts.jas.4.14: who do not know the thing of the morrow; for what is your life? for it is a vapour that is appearing for a little, and then is vanishing;
texts.jas.4.15: instead of your saying, `If the Lord may will, we shall live, and do this or that;'
texts.jas.4.16: and now ye glory in your pride; all such glorying is evil;
texts.jas.4.17: to him, then, knowing to do good, and not doing, sin it is to him.
texts.jas.5.1: Go, now, ye rich! weep, howling over your miseries that are coming upon [you];
texts.jas.5.2: your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten;
texts.jas.5.3: your gold and silver have rotted, and the rust of them for a testimony shall be to you, and shall eat your flesh as fire. Ye made treasure in the last days!
texts.jas.5.4: lo, the reward of the workmen, of those who in-gathered your fields, which hath been fraudulently kept back by you -- doth cry out, and the exclamations of those who did reap into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth have entered;
texts.jas.5.5: ye did live in luxury upon the earth, and were wanton; ye did nourish your hearts, as in a day of slaughter;
texts.jas.5.6: ye did condemn -- ye did murder the righteous one, he doth not resist you.
texts.jas.5.7: Be patient, then, brethren, till the presence of the Lord; lo, the husbandman doth expect the precious fruit of the earth, being patient for it, till he may receive rain -- early and latter;
texts.jas.5.8: be patient, ye also; establish your hearts, because the presence of the Lord hath drawn nigh;
texts.jas.5.9: murmur not against one another, brethren, that ye may not be condemned; lo, the Judge before the door hath stood.
texts.jas.5.10: An example take ye of the suffering of evil, my brethren, and of the patience, the prophets who did speak in the name of the Lord;
texts.jas.5.11: lo, we call happy those who are enduring; the endurance of Job ye heard of, and the end of the Lord ye have seen, that very compassionate is the Lord, and pitying.
texts.jas.5.12: And before all things, my brethren, do not swear, neither by the heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath, and let your Yes be Yes, and the No, No; that under judgment ye may not fall.
texts.jas.5.13: Doth any one suffer evil among you? let him pray; is any of good cheer? let him sing psalms;
texts.jas.5.14: is any infirm among you? let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, having anointed him with oil, in the name of the Lord,
texts.jas.5.15: and the prayer of the faith shall save the distressed one, and the Lord shall raise him up, and if sins he may have committed, they shall be forgiven to him.
texts.jas.5.16: Be confessing to one another the trespasses, and be praying for one another, that ye may be healed; very strong is a working supplication of a righteous man;
texts.jas.5.17: Elijah was a man like affected as we, and with prayer he did pray -- not to rain, and it did not rain upon the land three years and six months;
texts.jas.5.18: and again he did pray, and the heaven did give rain, and the land did bring forth her fruit.
texts.jas.5.19: Brethren, if any among you may go astray from the truth, and any one may turn him back,
texts.jas.5.20: let him know that he who did turn back a sinner from the straying of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall cover a multitude of sins.

texts.jas.1.1: Santiago siervo de Dios y del Señor Jesu Cristo, a las doce tribus que están en la dispersión, salud.
texts.jas.1.2: Hermanos míos, tenéd por todo gozo cuando cayereis en diversas tribulaciones:
texts.jas.1.3: Sabiendo que la prueba de vuestra fe obra paciencia.
texts.jas.1.4: Mas tenga la paciencia su obra perfecta, para que seáis perfectos y cabales, sin faltar en alguna cosa.
texts.jas.1.5: Y si alguno de vosotros tiene falta de sabiduría, demánde la a Dios, (el cual da a todos dadivosamente, y no zahiere,) y serle ha dada.
texts.jas.1.6: Empero demande en fe, no dudando nada; porque el que duda, es semejante a la onda de la mar, que es movida del viento, y es echada de una parte a otra.
texts.jas.1.7: No piense pues el tal hombre que recibirá cosa alguna del Señor.
texts.jas.1.8: El hombre de doblado ánimo, es inconstante en todos sus caminos.
texts.jas.1.9: Además, el hermano que es de humilde condición, gloríese en su ensalzamiento;
texts.jas.1.10: Mas el que es rico, en su humillación; porque él se pasará como la flor de la yerba:
texts.jas.1.11: Que salido el sol con ardor, la yerba se secó, y su flor se cayó, y su hermosa apariencia pereció: así también se marchitará el rico en sus caminos.
texts.jas.1.12: Bienaventurado el varón que sufre tentación; porque después que fuere probado, recibirá la corona de vida, que Dios ha prometido a los que le aman.
texts.jas.1.13: Cuando alguno es tentado, no diga, que Dios me tienta; porque Dios no puede ser tentado por el mal, ni él tienta a alguno:
texts.jas.1.14: Sino que cada uno es tentado, cuando de su propia concupiscencia es atraído, y cebado.
texts.jas.1.15: Y la concupiscencia después que ha concebido, pare al pecado: y el pecado, siendo cumplido, engendra muerte.
texts.jas.1.16: Hermanos míos muy amados, no erréis.
texts.jas.1.17: Toda buena dádiva, y todo don perfecto es de lo alto, que desciende del Padre de las lumbres, en el cual no hay mudanza, ni sombra de variación.
texts.jas.1.18: El de su propia voluntad nos ha engendrado por la palabra de verdad, para que seamos como primicias de sus criaturas.
texts.jas.1.19: Así que, hermanos míos muy amados, todo hombre sea pronto para oír, tardío para hablar, tardío para airarse;
texts.jas.1.20: Porque la ira del hombre no obra la justicia de Dios.
texts.jas.1.21: Por lo cual dejando toda inmundicia, y superfluidad de malicia, recibíd con mansedumbre la palabra injerida en vosotros, la cual puede hacer salvas vuestras almas.
texts.jas.1.22: Mas sed hacedores de la palabra, y no tan solamente oidores, engañándoos a vosotros mismos.
texts.jas.1.23: Porque si alguno oye la palabra, y no la pone por obra, este tal es semejante al hombre que considera en un espejo su rostro natural:
texts.jas.1.24: Porque él se consideró a sí mismo, y se fue; y luego se olvidó qué tal era.
texts.jas.1.25: Mas el que hubiere mirado atentamente en la ley perfecta que es la de la libertad, y hubiere perseverado en ella, no siendo oidor olvidadizo, sino hacedor de la obra, este tal será bienaventurado en su hecho.
texts.jas.1.26: Si alguno de entre vosotros piensa ser religioso, y no refrena su lengua, sino que engaña su propio corazón, la religión del tal es vana.
texts.jas.1.27: La religión pura y sin mácula delante de Dios y Padre es esta: Visitar los huérfanos y las viudas en sus tribulaciones, y guardarse sin mancha del mundo.
texts.jas.2.1: Hermanos míos, no tengáis la fe de nuestro Señor Jesu Cristo glorioso en acepción de personas.
texts.jas.2.2: Porque si en vuestra congregación entra algún varón, que trae anillo de oro, vestido de preciosa ropa, y también entra un pobre vestido de vestidura vil,
texts.jas.2.3: Y pusiereis los ojos en el que trae la vestidura preciosa, y le dijereis: Tú asiéntate aquí honorífica mente; y dijereis al pobre: Estáte tú allí en pie; o, siéntate aquí debajo del estrado de mis pies:
texts.jas.2.4: ¿Vosotros, no hacéis ciertamente distinción dentro de vosotros mismos, y sois hechos jueces de pensamientos malos?
texts.jas.2.5: Hermanos míos amados, oíd: ¿No ha elegido Dios los pobres de este mundo, que sean ricos en fe, y herederos del reino que ha prometido a los que le aman?
texts.jas.2.6: Mas vosotros habéis afrentado al pobre. ¿Los ricos no os oprimen con tiranía, y ellos mismos os arrastran a los juzgados?
texts.jas.2.7: ¿No blasfeman ellos el buen nombre que es invocado sobre vosotros?
texts.jas.2.8: Si ciertamente vosotros cumplís la ley real conforme a la Escritura, es a saber: Amarás a tu prójimo como a ti mismo; bien hacéis;
texts.jas.2.9: Mas si hacéis acepción de personas, cometéis pecado, y sois acusados de la ley como transgresores.
texts.jas.2.10: Porque cualquiera que hubiere guardado toda la ley, y sin embargo se deslizare en un punto, es hecho culpado de todos.
texts.jas.2.11: Porque el que dijo: No cometas adulterio, también ha dicho: No mates. Y si no hubieres cometido adulterio, empero hubieres matado, ya eres hecho transgresor de la ley.
texts.jas.2.12: Así hablád, y así obrád como los que habéis de ser juzgados por la ley de libertad.
texts.jas.2.13: Porque juicio sin misericordia será hecho a aquel que no hiciere misericordia; y la misericordia se gloría contra el juicio.
texts.jas.2.14: Hermanos míos, ¿qué aprovechará si alguno dice que tiene fe, y no tiene obras? ¿Podrá la fe salvarle?
texts.jas.2.15: Porque si el hermano, o la hermana estuvieren desnudos, o necesitados del mantenimiento de cada día,
texts.jas.2.16: Y alguno de vosotros les dijere: Id en paz, calentáos, y hartáos, empero no les diéreis las cosas que son necesarias para el cuerpo, ¿qué les aprovechará?
texts.jas.2.17: Así también la fe, si no tuviere obras, es muerta por sí misma.
texts.jas.2.18: Mas alguno dirá: Tú tienes fe, y yo tengo obras; muéstrame tu fe sin tus obras; y yo te mostraré mi fe por mis obras.
texts.jas.2.19: Tú crees que Dios es uno: haces bien: también los demonios lo creen, y tiemblan.
texts.jas.2.20: ¿Mas, oh hombre vano, quieres saber, que la fe sin las obras es muerta?
texts.jas.2.21: Abraham, nuestro padre, ¿no fue justificado por las obras, cuando ofreció a su hijo Isaac sobre el altar?
texts.jas.2.22: ¿ No ves que la fe obró con sus obras, y que por las obras la fe fue perfecta?
texts.jas.2.23: Y la Escritura fue cumplida, que dice: Abraham creyó a Dios, y le fue imputado a justicia, y fue llamado el amigo de Dios.
texts.jas.2.24: Vosotros, pues, veis, que por las obras es justificado el hombre, y no solamente por la fe.
texts.jas.2.25: Semejantemente también Raab la ramera, ¿no fue justificada por obras, cuando recibió los mensajeros, y los echó fuera por otro camino?
texts.jas.2.26: Porque como el cuerpo sin espíritu está muerto, así también la fe sin obras es muerta.
texts.jas.3.1: Hermanos míos, no os hagáis muchos de vosotros maestros, sabiendo que recibiremos mayor condenación.
texts.jas.3.2: Porque todos ofendemos en muchas cosas. Si alguno no ofende en palabra, éste es varón perfecto, que también puede con freno gobernar todo el cuerpo.
texts.jas.3.3: He aquí, nosotros ponemos a los caballos frenos en las bocas para que nos obedezcan, y gobernamos todo su cuerpo.
texts.jas.3.4: He aquí también las naos, siendo tan grandes, y siendo llevadas de impetuosos vientos, son sin embargo gobernadas con un muy pequeño gobernalle por donde quiera que quisiere la gana del que las gobierna.
texts.jas.3.5: Semejantemente también la lengua es un pequeñito miembro, mas se gloría de grandes cosas. He aquí, un pequeño fuego, ¡cuán grande bosque enciende!
texts.jas.3.6: Y la lengua es un fuego, digo, un mundo de maldad. Así la lengua está puesta entre nuestros miembros, la cual contamina todo el cuerpo, e inflama la rueda natural; y es inflamada del gehena.
texts.jas.3.7: Porque toda naturaleza de bestias fieras, y de aves, y de serpientes, y de los de la mar, se doma, y es domada por la naturaleza humana;
texts.jas.3.8: Pero ningún hombre puede domar la lengua: es un mal que no puede ser refrenado, y está llena de veneno mortal.
texts.jas.3.9: Con ella bendecimos a Dios, y al Padre, y con ella maldecimos a los hombres, los cuales son hechos a la semejanza de Dios.
texts.jas.3.10: De una misma boca procede bendición y maldición. Hermanos míos, no conviene que estas cosas sean así hechas.
texts.jas.3.11: ¿Echa alguna fuente por un mismo manantial agua dulce y amarga?
texts.jas.3.12: Hermanos míos, ¿puede la higuera producir aceitunas; o la vid, higos? Así ninguna fuente puede dar agua salada y dulce.
texts.jas.3.13: ¿Quién es sabio, y entendido entre vosotros? muestre por buena conversación sus obras en mansedumbre de sabiduría.
texts.jas.3.14: Empero si tenéis envidia amarga, y contención en vuestros corazones, no os glorieis, ni seáis mentirosos contra la verdad;
texts.jas.3.15: Porque esta sabiduría no es la que desciende de lo alto, sino que es terrena, animal, y demoniaca.
texts.jas.3.16: Porque donde hay envidia y contención, allí hay tumulto, y toda obra perversa.
texts.jas.3.17: Empero la sabiduría que es de lo alto, primeramente es pura, después pacífica, modesta, fácil de persuadir, llena de misericordia y de buenos frutos, no juzgadora, no fingida.
texts.jas.3.18: Y el fruto de justicia se siembra en paz para aquellos que hacen paz.
texts.jas.4.1: ¿De dónde vienen las guerras, y los pleitos entre vosotros? De aquí, es a saber, de vuestras concupiscencias, las cuales batallan en vuestros miembros.
texts.jas.4.2: Codiciáis, y no tenéis: tenéis envidia y odio, y no podéis alcanzar: combatís y guerreáis, empero no tenéis lo que deseáis, porque no pedís.
texts.jas.4.3: Pedís, y no recibís; porque pedís malamente, para gastar en vuestros deleites.
texts.jas.4.4: Adúlteros y adúlteras, ¿no sabéis que la amistad del mundo es enemistad con Dios? Cualquiera, pues, que quisiere ser amigo del mundo, se constituye enemigo de Dios.
texts.jas.4.5: ¿Pensáis que la Escritura dice sin causa: El espíritu que mora en nosotros, codicia envidiosamente?
texts.jas.4.6: Mas él da mayor gracia. Porque él dice: Dios resiste a los soberbios, empero da gracia a los humildes.
texts.jas.4.7: Sed pues sujetos a Dios: resistíd al diablo, y huirá de vosotros.
texts.jas.4.8: Allegáos a Dios, y él se allegará a vosotros. Pecadores, limpiád las manos; y vosotros de doblado ánimo, purificád los corazones.
texts.jas.4.9: Afligíos, y lamentád, y llorád. Vuestra risa conviértase en lloro, y vuestro gozo en tristeza.
texts.jas.4.10: Humilláos delante de la presencia del Señor, y él os ensalzará.
texts.jas.4.11: Hermanos, no digáis mal los unos de los otros: el que dice mal de su hermano, y juzga a su hermano, este tal dice mal de la ley, y juzga a la ley; mas si tú juzgas a la ley, no eres guardador de la ley, sino juez.
texts.jas.4.12: Solo uno es el dador de la ley, que puede salvar, y perder: ¿Quién eres tú que juzgas a otro?
texts.jas.4.13: Ea ahora, vosotros los que decís: Vamos hoy y mañana a tal ciudad, y estaremos allá un año, y compraremos mercadería, y ganarémos:
texts.jas.4.14: Vosotros que no sabéis lo que será mañana. Porque, ¿qué es vuestra vida? Ciertamente es un vapor que se aparece por un poco de tiempo, y después se desvanece.
texts.jas.4.15: En lugar de lo cual deberíais decir: Si el Señor quisiere, y si viviéremos, haremos esto o aquello.
texts.jas.4.16: Mas ahora triunfáis en vuestras soberbias. Toda gloria semejante es mala.
texts.jas.4.17: El pecado, pues, está en aquel que sabe hacer lo bueno, y no lo hace.
texts.jas.5.1: Ea ya ahora, ricos, llorád aullando por causa de las miserias que os han de sobrevenir.
texts.jas.5.2: Vuestras riquezas están podridas; y vuestras ropas están roidas de la polilla.
texts.jas.5.3: Vuestro oro y vuestra plata están orinecidos, y el orín de ellos será testimonio contra vosotros, y comerá del todo vuestras carnes como fuego: habéis allegado tesoro para en los postreros días.
texts.jas.5.4: He aquí, el jornal de los obreros que han segado vuestras tierras, (el cual por engaño no les ha sido pagado de vosotros,) clama; y los clamores de los que habían segado han entrado en el oído del Señor de los ejércitos.
texts.jas.5.5: Habéis vivido en deleites sobre la tierra, y sido disolutos, y habéis cebado vuestros corazones como en un día de matanza.
texts.jas.5.6: Habéis condenado y muerto al justo, y él no os resiste.
texts.jas.5.7: Por tanto, hermanos, sed pacientes hasta la venida del Señor. He aquí, el labrador espera el precioso fruto de la tierra, esperando pacientemente, hasta que reciba la lluvia temprana y tardía.
texts.jas.5.8: Sed pues también vosotros pacientes, y fortificád vuestros corazones; porque la venida del Señor se acerca.
texts.jas.5.9: Hermanos, no gimáis unos contra otros, porque no seáis condenados: He aquí, el juez está delante de la puerta.
texts.jas.5.10: Hermanos míos, tomád por ejemplo de sufrir el mal, y de paciencia, a los profetas que hablaron en el nombre del Señor.
texts.jas.5.11: He aquí, tenemos por bienaventurados a los que sufren. Vosotros habéis oído de la paciencia de Job, y habéis visto el fin del Señor, que el Señor es muy misericordioso y piadoso.
texts.jas.5.12: Empero, hermanos míos, ante todas cosas no juréis, ni por el cielo, ni por la tierra, ni por otro cualquier juramento; mas vuestro Sí, sea Sí; y vuestro No, No; porque no caigáis en condenación.
texts.jas.5.13: ¿Está alguno entre vosotros afligido? haga oración. ¿Está alguno alegre entre vosotros? salmodie.
texts.jas.5.14: ¿Está alguno enfermo entre vosotros? llame a los ancianos de la iglesia, y oren sobre él, ungiéndole con aceite en el nombre del Señor;
texts.jas.5.15: Y la oración de fe hará salvo al enfermo, y el Señor le aliviará; y si estuviere en pecados, le serán perdonados.
texts.jas.5.16: Confesáos vuestras faltas unos a otros, y rogád los unos por los otros, para que seáis sanos. La oración eficaz del justo puede mucho.
texts.jas.5.17: Elías era hombre sujeto a semejantes pasiones que nosotros, y rogó con oración que no lloviese, y no llovió sobre la tierra por tres años, y seis meses.
texts.jas.5.18: Y otra vez oró, y el cielo dio lluvia, y la tierra produjo su fruto.
texts.jas.5.19: Hermanos, si alguno de entre vosotros errare de la verdad, y alguno le convirtiere,
texts.jas.5.20: Sepa este tal que el que hubiere hecho convertir al pecador del error de su camino, salvará un alma de muerte, y cubrirá multitud de pecados.

texts.jas.1.1: James, a servant, of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ,—unto the twelve tribes that are in the dispersion, Wishes joy.
texts.jas.1.2: All Joy, account it, my brethren, whensoever ye fall in with, manifold, temptations,—
texts.jas.1.3: Taking note, that, the proving of your faith, worketh out endurance;
texts.jas.1.4: But let, your endurance, have, mature work, that ye may be mature and complete, in nothing, coming short.
texts.jas.1.5: But, if any of you is sinning short of wisdom, let him be asking of God, Who giveth unto all freely and upbraideth not, and it shall be given him;
texts.jas.1.6: But let him be asking in faith, nothing, doubting, for, he that doubteth, is like a wave of the sea, wind-driven and storm-tossed,—
texts.jas.1.7: For let not that man think that he shall receive anything from the Lord—
texts.jas.1.8: A two-souled man, unstable in all his ways.
texts.jas.1.9: But boasting be the lowly brother in his uplifting;
texts.jas.1.10: Whereas the rich, in his being brought low,—because, as a flower of grass, he will pass away;
texts.jas.1.11: For the sun hath sprung up, with it scorching heat, and hath withered the grass, and, the flower thereof, hath fallen out, and, the beauty of the face thereof, hath perished,—so, also the rich, in his goings, shall languish.
texts.jas.1.12: Happy the man who endureth temptation! Because, becoming approved, he shall receive the crown of life—which he hath promised unto them that love him.
texts.jas.1.13: Let, no one, while tempted, be saying—From God, am I tempted,—for, God, cannot be tempted by things evil, and, himself, tempteth no one;
texts.jas.1.14: But, each one, is tempted, when, by his own coveting, he is drawn out and enticed,
texts.jas.1.15: Then, the coveting, having conceived, giveth birth to sin, and, the sin, when full-grown, bringeth forth death.
texts.jas.1.16: Be not deceived, my brethren beloved:—
texts.jas.1.17: Every good giving, and every perfect gift, is, from above, coming down from the Father of lights—with whom is no alternation, nor shadow cast, by turning:
texts.jas.1.18: Because he was so minded, he hath brought us forth with a word of truth, to the end we should be a sort of firstfruit of his creatures
texts.jas.1.19: Ye know, my brethren beloved,—but let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,
texts.jas.1.20: For, man’s anger, worketh not, God’s righteousness.
texts.jas.1.21: Wherefore, putting away all filthiness and overflow of baseness, in meekness, welcome ye the word fitted for inward growth, which is able to save your souls:
texts.jas.1.22: Become ye doers of the word, and not hearers only—reasoning yourselves astray;
texts.jas.1.23: Because, if any is, a word-hearer, and not a doer, the same, is like unto a man observing his natural face in a mirror,—
texts.jas.1.24: For he observed himself, and is gone away, and, straightway, it hath escaped him,—what manner of man, he was!
texts.jas.1.25: But, he that hath obtained a nearer view into the perfect law of liberty, and hath taken up his abode by it, becoming—not a forgetful hearer, but a work doer, the same, happy in his doing, shall be.
texts.jas.1.26: If any thinketh he is observant of religion, not curbing his own tongue, but deceiving his own heart, this one’s, religious observance is, vain:
texts.jas.1.27: Religious observance, pure and undefiled with our God and Father, is, this—to be visiting orphans and widows in their affliction, unspotted, to keep, himself, from the world.
texts.jas.2.1: My brethren, do not, with respect for persons, be holding the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, [the Lord] of glory.
texts.jas.2.2: For, if there enter into your synagogue a man wearing gold rings in gay clothing, and there enter a destitute man also, in soiled clothing,—
texts.jas.2.3: And ye eye him that hath on the gay clothing, and say, Thou, be sitting here, pleasantly,—and, unto the destitute man, say—Thou, stand, or sit there under my footstool,
texts.jas.2.4: Would ye not have been led to make distinctions among yourselves, and have become judges with wicked reasonings?
texts.jas.2.5: Hearken! my brethren beloved:—Hath not, God, chosen the destitute in the world [to be] rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?
texts.jas.2.6: Whereas, ye, have dishonoured the destitute man! Do not, the rich, oppress you? and, themselves, drag you into courts of justice?
texts.jas.2.7: Do not, they, defame the noble name which hath been invoked upon you?
texts.jas.2.8: If ye are, indeed, fulfilling, a royal law, according to the scripture—Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, nobly, are ye doing;
texts.jas.2.9: But, if ye are shewing respect of persons, sin, are ye working, being convicted by the law as transgressors!
texts.jas.2.10: For, a man who shall keep, the whole law, but shall stumble in one thing, hath become, for all things, liable,—
texts.jas.2.11: For, he that hath said—Do not commit adultery, hath also said—Do not commit murder,—now, if thou dost not commit adultery, but dost commit murder, thou hast become a transgressor of law.
texts.jas.2.12: So, be speaking, and, so, doing, as they who, through means of a law of freedom, are about to be judged;
texts.jas.2.13: For, the judgment, [will be] without mercy, unto him that hath shewed no mercy: Mercy, boasteth, over judgment.
texts.jas.2.14: What profit, my brethren,—if one should be saying he hath, faith, but hath not, works; can his faith save him?
texts.jas.2.15: If, a brother or sister, should be naked, and coming short of the daily food,
texts.jas.2.16: And one from among you should say unto them—Withdraw in peace, be getting warmed and fed, but should not give them the things needful for the body, What the profit?
texts.jas.2.17: So, also, faith, if it have not works, is dead, by itself.
texts.jas.2.18: But one will say,—Thou, hast faith, and, I, have works, show me thy faith apart from thy works, and, I, unto thee, will shew, by my works, my faith.
texts.jas.2.19: Thou believest that God is, one: thou doest, well—Even the demons believe, and shudder!
texts.jas.2.20: But art thou willing to learn, O empty man! that, faith, apart from works, is, idle?
texts.jas.2.21: Abraham our father, was it not, by works, he was declared righteous—when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
texts.jas.2.22: Thou seest that, his faith, had been working together with his works, and by his works did his faith become full-grown,—
texts.jas.2.23: And the scripture was fulfilled which saith—And Abraham believed God, And it was reckoned to him as righteousness, and, God’s friend, was he called:
texts.jas.2.24: Ye see that—by works, a man is declared righteous, and not by faith alone.
texts.jas.2.25: And, in like manner also, Rahab the harlot, Was it not, by works, she was declared righteous, when she gave welcome unto the messengers, and, by another way, urged them forth?
texts.jas.2.26: Just as, the body, apart from spirit, is dead, so, our faith also, apart from works, is dead.
texts.jas.3.1: Not, many teachers, become ye, my brethren, knowing that, a severer sentence, shall ye receive;
texts.jas.3.2: For, oft, are we stumbling, one and all: If anyone, in word, doth not stumble, the same, is a mature man, able to curb even the whole body.
texts.jas.3.3: Now, if, the horses bits, into their mouths, we thrust, to the end they may be yielding to us, their whole body also, do we turn about.
texts.jas.3.4: Lo! the ships also, large as they are, and, by rough winds, driven along, are turned about by a very small helm, whithersoever the impulse of the steersman inclineth.
texts.jas.3.5: So, also, the tongue, is, a little member, and yet, of great things, maketh boast. Lo! how small a fire, kindleth, how great a forest;
texts.jas.3.6: And, the tongue, is a fire,—[as], the world of unrighteousness, the tongue, becometh fixed among our members, that which defileth the whole body and setteth on fire the wheel of our natural life, and is set on fire, by gehenna!
texts.jas.3.7: For, every nature—both of wild beasts and of birds, both of reptiles and of things in the sea, is to be tamed, and hath been tamed, by the human nature;
texts.jas.3.8: But, the tongue, none of mankind can, tame,—A restless mischief! Full of deadly poison
texts.jas.3.9: Therewith, are we blessing our Lord and Father, and, therewith, we are cursing the men who, after the likeness of God, have been brought into being!
texts.jas.3.10: Out of the same mouth, come forth blessing and cursing! Not meet, my brethren, for, these things, thus, to be coming to pass!
texts.jas.3.11: Doth, the fountain, out of the same opening, teem forth the sweet and the bitter?
texts.jas.3.12: Is it possible, my brethren, for, a fig-tree, to produce, olives, or, a vine, figs? Neither can, salt, water yield, sweet.
texts.jas.3.13: Who is wise and well-instructed among you? Let him show, out of his comely behaviour, his works, in meekness of wisdom.
texts.jas.3.14: But, if, bitter jealousy, ye have, and rivalry, in your hearts; be not boasting and showing yourselves false against the truth!
texts.jas.3.15: This wisdom is not one, from above, coming down, but is earthly, born of the soul, demoniacal!
texts.jas.3.16: For, where jealousy and rivalry are, there, are anarchy and every ignoble deed.
texts.jas.3.17: But, the wisdom from above, is—first pure, then peaceable, reasonable, easy to be entreated, fraught with mercy and good fruits, without partiality, without hypocrisy.
texts.jas.3.18: And, in harvest of righteousness, with peace, is sown by them that make peace.
texts.jas.4.1: Whence wars and whence fightings among you? are they not from hence—due to your pleasures which are taking the field in your members?
texts.jas.4.2: Ye covet—and have not, ye commit murder, and are jealous—and cannot obtain,—ye fight and war. Ye have not—because ye do not really ask,
texts.jas.4.3: Ye ask and receive not, because that, basely, ye ask, in order that, in your pleasures, ye may spend [it].
texts.jas.4.4: Adulteresses! Know ye not that, the friendship of the world, is, enmity to God? Whosoever, therefore, is minded to be, a friend, of the world, an enemy of God, doth constitute himself.
texts.jas.4.5: Or think ye that, in vain, the scripture speaketh? Is it, for envying, that the spirit which hath taken an abode within us doth crave?
texts.jas.4.6: Howbeit he giveth, greater, favour. Wherefore it saith—God, against the haughty, arrayeth himself, Whereas, unto the lowly, he giveth favour.
texts.jas.4.7: Range yourselves, therefore, under God, but withstand the adversary, and he will flee from you:
texts.jas.4.8: Draw near unto God, and he will draw near unto you. Cleanse hands, sinners! Chasten hearts, double souls!
texts.jas.4.9: Be miserable and lament and weep, let, your laughter, into lamentation, be turned, and, your joy, into dejection;
texts.jas.4.10: Be made low in presence of the Lord, and he will lift you up.
texts.jas.4.11: Be not speaking one against another, brethren! He that speaketh against a brother, or judgeth his brother, speaketh against law, and judgeth law; Now, if, upon law, thou art passing judgment, thou art not a doer of law, but a judge!
texts.jas.4.12: One, is Lawgiver and Judge—He who hath power to save and to destroy; but who art, thou, that judgest thy neighbour?
texts.jas.4.13: Come now! ye that say—Today or To-morrow, we will journey unto this city here, and will spend there a year, and will trade and get gain,—
texts.jas.4.14: Men who are not versed in the morrow—of what sort your life [will be]; for ye are, a vapour—for a little, appearing, then, just disappearing!
texts.jas.4.15: Instead of your saying—If, the Lord, be pleased, we shall both, live and do this or that;
texts.jas.4.16: Whereas, now, are ye boasting in your pretensions:—All boasting like this, is, wicked,
texts.jas.4.17: To him, therefore, who knoweth how to be doing, a right thing, and is not doing it, it is, sin, unto him.
texts.jas.5.1: Come now! ye wealthy! Weep ye, howling, for your hardships which are coming upon you:
texts.jas.5.2: Your wealth, hath rotted, and, your garments, have become, moth-eaten,—
texts.jas.5.3: Your gold and silver, have rusted away, and, their rust, shall be, witness against you, and shall eat your flesh, as fire! Ye have laid up treasure in days of extremity:—
texts.jas.5.4: Lo, the wage of the workers who have out down your fields—that which hath been kept back, by you, is crying out; and, the outcries of them who reaped, into the ears of the Lord of hosts, have entered:
texts.jas.5.5: Ye have luxuriated upon the land, and run riot, ye have pampered your hearts in a day of slaughter;
texts.jas.5.6: Ye sentenced—ye murdered the Righteous one! Is he not arraying himself against you?
texts.jas.5.7: Be patient, therefore, brethren, until the Presence of the Lord:—Lo! the husbandman, awaiteth the precious fruit of the earth, having patience for it, until it receive the early and the latter rain:
texts.jas.5.8: Be, ye also, patient, Stablish your hearts, because, the Presence of the Lord, hath drawn near.
texts.jas.5.9: Be not sighing, brethren, one against another, lest ye be judged,—Lo! the Judge, before the doors, is standing.
texts.jas.5.10: An example, take ye, brethren, of distress and patience,—the prophets who have spoken in the name of the Lord.
texts.jas.5.11: Lo! we pronounce them happy who have endured;—Of the endurance of Job, ye have heard, and, the end of the Lord, have ye seen,—that, of much tender affection, is the Lord, and full of compassion,
texts.jas.5.12: But, before all things, my brethren, do not swear,—either by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your Yea be yea, and your Nay nay,—lest, under judgment, ye fall.
texts.jas.5.13: In distress, is any among you? Let him pray; Cheerful, is any? Let him strike the strings;
texts.jas.5.14: Sick, is any among you? Let him call unto him the elders of the assembly, and let them pray for him, anointing him with oil in the name [of the Lord];—
texts.jas.5.15: And, the prayer of faith, shall save the exhausted one, and the Lord will raise him up, and, if he have committed, sins, it shall be forgiven him.
texts.jas.5.16: Be openly confessing, therefore, one to another, your sins, and be praying in each other’s behalf,—that ye may be healed. Much availeth, the supplication of a righteous man, when it is energised:
texts.jas.5.17: Elijah, was, a man, affected like us; and he earnestly prayed that there might be no moisture, and there was no moisture on the land, for three years and six months,—
texts.jas.5.18: And, again, he prayed, and, the heaven, gave, rain, and, the land, shot up her fruit.
texts.jas.5.19: My brethren! If one among you be led to err from the truth, and one turn him back,
texts.jas.5.20: Be ye taking note—that, he that turneth back a sinner out of the error of his way—will save his soul out of death, and hide a multitude of sins.

texts.jas.1.1: Santiago, siervo de Dios y del Señor Jesucristo, a las doce tribus que están en la Dispersión: Saludos.
texts.jas.1.2: Hermanos míos, estad contentos cuando caigáis en diversas pruebas,
texts.jas.1.3: sabiendo que la prueba de vuestra fe produce paciencia.
texts.jas.1.4: Dejad que la paciencia tenga su obra perfecta, para que seáis perfectos y cabales, sin que os falte nada.
texts.jas.1.5: Pero si a alguno de vosotros le falta sabiduría, pídala a Dios, que da a todos con liberalidad y sin reproche, y le será concedida.
texts.jas.1.6: Pero que pida con fe, sin dudar, porque el que duda es como la ola del mar, impulsada por el viento y zarandeada.
texts.jas.1.7: Porque ese hombre no debe pensar que recibirá algo del Señor.
texts.jas.1.8: Es un hombre de doble ánimo, inestable en todos sus caminos.
texts.jas.1.9: Que el hermano de condición humilde se gloríe en su alta posición;
texts.jas.1.10: y el rico, en su humillación, porque como la flor de la hierba, pasará.
texts.jas.1.11: Porque el sol se levanta con el viento abrasador y marchita la hierba; y su flor cae, y la belleza de su aspecto perece. Así también el rico se desvanecerá en sus caminos.
texts.jas.1.12: Bienaventurado el varón que soporta la tentación, porque cuando haya sido aprobado, recibirá la corona de la vida que el Señor prometió a los que le aman.
texts.jas.1.13: Que nadie diga cuando es tentado: «Soy tentado por Dios», porque Dios no puede ser tentado por el mal, y él mismo no tienta a nadie.
texts.jas.1.14: Pero cada uno es tentado cuando es atraído por su propia concupiscencia y seducido.
texts.jas.1.15: Entonces la concupiscencia, cuando ha concebido, engendra el pecado. El pecado, cuando ha crecido, produce la muerte.
texts.jas.1.16: No os dejéis engañar, mis amados hermanos.
texts.jas.1.17: Toda buena dádiva y todo don perfecto viene de lo alto, del Padre de las luces, en quien no puede haber variación ni sombra de cambio.
texts.jas.1.18: De su propia voluntad nos hizo nacer por la palabra de la verdad, para que seamos una especie de primicias de sus criaturas.
texts.jas.1.19: Así que, mis amados hermanos, todo hombre sea pronto para oír, tardo para hablar y tardo para la ira;
texts.jas.1.20: porque la ira del hombre no produce la justicia de Dios.
texts.jas.1.21: Por tanto, desechando toda inmundicia y abundancia de maldad, recibid con mansedumbre la palabra implantada, la cual puede salvar vuestras almas.
texts.jas.1.22: Pero sed hacedores de la palabra, y no sólo oidores, engañándoos a vosotros mismos.
texts.jas.1.23: Porque si alguno es oidor de la palabra y no hacedor, es como un hombre que mira su rostro natural en un espejo;
texts.jas.1.24: porque se ve a sí mismo, y se va, y enseguida se olvida de la clase de hombre que era.
texts.jas.1.25: Pero el que mira atentamente en la perfecta ley, la de la libertad, y persevera en ella, no siendo un oidor olvidadizo, sino un hacedor de la obra, este será bienaventurado en lo que hace.
texts.jas.1.26: Si alguno de vosotros se cree religioso mientras no refrena su lengua, sino que engaña a su corazón, la religión de ese hombre es vana.
texts.jas.1.27: La religión pura y sin mácula ante Dios el Padre es esta: visitar a los huérfanos y a las viudas en sus tribulaciones, y guardarse sin mancha del mundo.
texts.jas.2.1: Hermanos míos, no tengáis la fe de nuestro glorioso Señor Jesucristo con acepción de personas.
texts.jas.2.2: Porque si entra en vuestra congregación un hombre con un anillo de oro, vestido con ropas finas, y entra también un pobre vestido con ropas sucias,
texts.jas.2.3: y os fijáis especialmente en el que lleva las ropas finas y le decís: «Siéntate aquí en un buen lugar», y al pobre le decís: «Ponte ahí de pie», o «Siéntate junto al escabel de mis pies»
texts.jas.2.4: ¿no habéis hecho distinciones entre vosotros, y os habéis convertido en jueces con malos pensamientos?
texts.jas.2.5: Escuchad, mis amados hermanos. ¿No ha elegido Dios a los pobres de este mundo para que sean ricos en la fe y herederos del Reino que prometió a los que le aman?
texts.jas.2.6: Pero vosotros habéis deshonrado al pobre. ¿No os oprimen los ricos y son ellos los que os arrastran ante los tribunales?
texts.jas.2.7: ¿No blasfeman ellos el honorable nombre que fue invocado sobre vosotros?
texts.jas.2.8: Sin embargo, si cumplís la ley real según la Escritura: «Amarás a tu prójimo como a ti mismo», hacéis bien.
texts.jas.2.9: Pero si hacéis acepción de personas, cometéis pecado, y sois condenados por la ley como transgresores.
texts.jas.2.10: Porque el que guarda toda la ley y tropieza en un punto, se hace culpable de todos.
texts.jas.2.11: Porque el que dijo: «No cometas adulterio», también dijo: «No cometas homicidio». Ahora bien, si no cometes adulterio pero cometes homicidio, te has convertido en transgresor de la ley.
texts.jas.2.12: Así hablad y así haced, como quienes han de ser juzgados por la ley de la libertad.
texts.jas.2.13: Porque el juicio será sin misericordia para el que no ha mostrado misericordia. La misericordia triunfa sobre el juicio.
texts.jas.2.14: ¿De qué sirve, hermanos míos, que alguno diga que tiene fe, pero no tenga obras? ¿Acaso esa fe puede salvarle?
texts.jas.2.15: Y si un hermano o una hermana están desnudos y les falta el alimento de cada día,
texts.jas.2.16: y uno de vosotros les dice: «Id en paz. Calentaos y saciaos»; pero no les dais lo que necesita el cuerpo, ¿de qué sirve?
